tasks.help: Pushes a package to the server and publishes it.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: Path of the package to push.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: Specifies the server URL. This option is required unless <c>DefaultPushSource</c> config value is set in the NuGet config file.

properties.name: SymbolSource
properties.help: Specifies the symbol server URL.

properties.name: Timeout
properties.help: Specifies the timeout for pushing to a server in seconds. Defaults to 300 seconds (5 minutes). Specifying 0 (zero seconds) applies the default value.

properties.name: ApiKey
properties.help: The API key for the server.

properties.name: SymbolApiKey
properties.help: The API key for the symbol server.

properties.name: DisableBuffering
properties.help: Disables buffering when pushing to an HTTP(S) server to decrease memory usage.

properties.name: NoSymbols
properties.help: Doesn't push symbols (even if present).

properties.name: ForceEnglishOutput
properties.help: Forces all logged output in English.

properties.name: SkipDuplicate
properties.help: When pushing multiple packages to an HTTP(S) server, treats any 409 Conflict response as a warning so that the push can continue. Available since .NET Core 3.1 SDK.

properties.name: NoServiceEndpoint
properties.help: Doesn't append <c>api/v2/package</c> to the source URL. Option available since .NET Core 2.1 SDK.

tasks.help: The dotnet nuget delete command deletes or unlists a package from the server. For nuget.org, the action is to unlist the package.

properties.name: PackageId
properties.help: Package Id to delete. The exact behavior depends on the source. For local folders, for instance, the package is deleted; for nuget.org the package is unlisted.

properties.name: PackageVersion
properties.help: Package Version to delete. The exact behavior depends on the source. For local folders, for instance, the package is deleted; for nuget.org the package is unlisted.

properties.name: Source
properties.help: Specifies the server URL. This option is required unless <c>DefaultPushSource</c> config value is set in the NuGet config file.

properties.name: ApiKey
properties.help: The API key for the server.

properties.name: ForceEnglishOutput
properties.help: Forces all logged output in English.

properties.name: NoServiceEndpoint
properties.help: Doesn't append <c>api/v2/package</c> to the source URL. Option available since .NET Core 2.1 SDK.

properties.name: Interactive
properties.help: Allows the command to stop and wait for user input or action. For example, to complete authentication. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.

properties.name: NonInteractive
properties.help: Doesn't prompt for user input or confirmations.

tasks.help: The dotnet nuget sign command signs all the packages matching the first argument with a certificate. The certificate with the private key can be obtained from a file or from a certificate installed in a certificate store by providing a subject name or a SHA-1 fingerprint.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: Path of the package to sign.

properties.name: CertificatePath
properties.help: Specifies the file path to the certificate to be used in signing the package.

properties.name: CertificateStoreName
properties.help: Specifies the name of the X.509 certificate store to use to search for the certificate. Defaults to 'My', the X.509 certificate store for personal certificates. This option should be used when specifying the certificate via --certificate-subject-name or --certificate-fingerprint options.

properties.name: CertificateStoreLocation
properties.help: Specifies the name of the X.509 certificate store use to search for the certificate. Defaults to 'CurrentUser', the X.509 certificate store used by the current user. This option should be used when specifying the certificate via --certificate-subject-name or --certificate-fingerprint options.

properties.name: CertificateSubjectName
properties.help: Specifies the subject name of the certificate used to search a local certificate store for the certificate. The search is a case-insensitive string comparison using the supplied value, which finds all certificates with the subject name containing that string, regardless of other subject values. The certificate store can be specified by --certificate-store-name and --certificate-store-location options.

properties.name: CertificateFingerprint
properties.help: Specifies the fingerprint of the certificate used to search a local certificate store for the certificate. Starting with .NET 9, this option can be used to specify the SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 fingerprint of the certificate. However, a NU3043 warning is raised when a SHA-1 certificate fingerprint is used because it is no longer considered secure.

properties.name: CertificatePassword
properties.help: Specifies the certificate password, if needed. If a certificate is password protected but no password is provided, the sign command will fail.

properties.name: HashAlgorithm
properties.help: Hash algorithm to be used to sign the package. Defaults to SHA256. Possible values are SHA256, SHA384, and SHA512.

properties.name: Output
properties.help: Specifies the directory where the signed package should be saved. If this option isn't specified, by default the original package is overwritten by the signed package.

properties.name: Overwrite
properties.help: Indicate that the current signature should be overwritten. By default the command will fail if the package already has a signature.

properties.name: TimestampHashAlgorithm
properties.help: Hash algorithm to be used by the RFC 3161 timestamp server. Defaults to SHA256.

properties.name: Timestamper
properties.help: URL to an RFC 3161 timestamping server.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

tasks.help: The dotnet nuget verify command verifies a signed NuGet package.

properties.name: TargetPath
properties.help: Path of the package to verify.

properties.name: CertificateFingerprint
properties.help: Verify that the signer certificate matches with one of the specified SHA256 fingerprints. This option can be supplied multiple times to provide multiple fingerprints.

properties.name: ConfigFile
properties.help: The NuGet configuration file (nuget.config) to use.

properties.name: Verbosity
properties.help: Sets the verbosity level of the command. Allowed values are <c>q[uiet]</c>, <c>m[inimal]</c>, <c>n[ormal]</c>, <c>d[etailed]</c>, and <c>diag[nostic]</c>.

commonTaskProperties.name: Properties
commonTaskProperties.help:
Set or override the specified project-level properties, where name is the property name and value is the property value. Specify each property separately, or use a semicolon or comma to separate multiple properties, as the following example shows:

--property:WarningLevel=2;OutDir=bin\Debug

delegates.name: PublishReadyToRun
delegates.help: Compiles application assemblies as ReadyToRun (R2R) format. R2R is a form of ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation. For more information, see ReadyToRun images. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

delegates.name: PublishSingleFile
delegates.help: Packages the app into a platform-specific single-file executable. The executable is self-extracting and contains all dependencies (including native) that are required to run the app. When the app is first run, the application is extracted to a directory based on the app name and build identifier. Startup is faster when the application is run again. The application doesn't need to extract itself a second time unless a new version is used. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK. For more information about single-file publishing, see the single-file bundler design document.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

delegates.name: PublishTrimmed
delegates.help: Trims unused libraries to reduce the deployment size of an app when publishing a self-contained executable. For more information, see Trim self-contained deployments and executables. Available since .NET Core 3.0 SDK as a preview feature.We recommend that you specify this option in a publish profile rather than on the command line. For more information, see MSBuild.

restore.name: DisableParallel
restore.help: Disables restoring multiple projects in parallel.

restore.name: Force
restore.help: Forces all dependencies to be resolved even if the last restore was successful. This is equivalent to deleting the project.assets.json file.

restore.name: IgnoreFailedSources
restore.help: Only warn about failed sources if there are packages meeting the version requirement.

restore.name: NoCache
restore.help: Specifies to not cache packages and HTTP requests.

restore.name: NoDependencies
restore.help: When restoring a project with project-to-project (P2P) references, restore the root project and not the references.

restore.name: PackageDirectory
restore.help: Specifies the directory for restored packages.

restore.name: Sources
restore.help: Specifies a NuGet package source to use during the restore operation. This overrides all of the sources specified in the NuGet.config file(s). Multiple sources can be provided by specifying this option multiple times.

restore.name: UseLockFile
restore.help: Enables project lock file to be generated and used with restore.

restore.name: LockedMode
restore.help: Don't allow updating project lock file.

restore.name: LockFilePath
restore.help: Output location where project lock file is written. By default, this is 'PROJECT_ROOT\packages.lock.json'.

restore.name: ForceEvaluate
restore.help: Forces restore to reevaluate all dependencies even if a lock file already exists.

restore-runtime.name: Runtime
restore-runtime.help: Specifies a runtime for the package restore. This is used to restore packages for runtimes not explicitly listed in the <RuntimeIdentifiers> tag in the .csproj file. For a list of Runtime Identifiers (RIDs), see the RID catalog. Provide multiple RIDs by specifying this option multiple times.
